unasked_decisions: QS-2 environment set to 'at the pitch'. The architect gave only '5 volunteers with 3 check-outs each'.
R-4 is mapped into QG-1 (functional completeness) and R-5 is listed under QG-1 without the architect discussing it. This is minor, because the architect confirmed the goal candidates in general.
Round 1 presented invented answers (20–30 coaches, laptop user, free hosting, history deleted each season) as pre-filled responses. The architect corrected all of them, and none reached the files.
extras: Offline conflict rule: the first sync wins and the second check-out is flagged for the kit manager (in QS-3).
Phone numbers are visible only to the kit manager, and only for overdue or lost items (in the stakeholders table).
No-login decision recorded as an accountability risk (QG-4) in section 11.
Offline view shows the last-synced holder and time, recorded as a risk to R-2.
Measurable successor scenario QS-5: 2 hours of reading the docs, then one change made and tested.
Usability test QS-2: 5 non-tech-savvy volunteers × 3 check-outs, 15 of 15 must pass.
Extra out-of-scope items: purchasing, membership and player records, integrations in v1.
ADR 0001 lists the central decisions: storage format, sync protocol, CSV format and versioning, QR payload, dependencies.

Gaps in the files: the 7-day overdue rule (Q11) and the kit-manager-only lost declaration (Q12) were agreed but not written. ADR 0001 is still 'proposed' and R-2 still has the old wording, because the final approval came after the last write.
